diagnostic.title: Format diagnostic report
diagnostic.intro: Use this when a file does not open or opens wrongly. TRACE reads the file on this computer and writes a short report about its structure, which you can send to the developers. Nothing is uploaded, and the file itself is never part of the report.
diagnostic.running: Analysing the file on this computer…
diagnostic.stalled: This is taking longer than expected. You can wait or cancel.
diagnostic.stopped: The analysis was stopped because it made no progress for {seconds} seconds.
diagnostic.workerFailed: The analysis could not be completed.
diagnostic.readFailed: The file could not be read.
diagnostic.incApp: The TRACE version and the family of your operating system (Windows, macOS or Linux).
diagnostic.incFile: The file extension, a size range (a power of two), the number and extensions of companion files, whether it is text or binary, its encoding and line endings, and a rough randomness profile of the bytes.
diagnostic.incDetection: Which of TRACE’s readers recognised the file, how sure each one was, and, for a failure, only a short error code and the step where it stopped.
diagnostic.incStructure: How often the format’s own keywords and section markers occur, how many fields each kind of line has, and the order of magnitude and number of decimal places of the numbers.
diagnostic.incResult: If the file opened: the numbers of parts, pins and nets rounded to two significant digits, and a few shares (for example pins without a net).
diagnostic.incChecks: Plausibility checks: how the board would look if the units, the pad angles or the bottom side were read differently, as counts and shares.
diagnostic.incPerformance: How long the reading took and a rough memory size.
diagnostic.incLevel2: Level 2: the shape of the first lines of each section (every run of letters becomes A, every run of digits 9, punctuation stays) and the tag and length of the first 256 binary blocks.
diagnostic.incDedupe: A short code that lets the developers recognise the same file if you send it twice. It is made with a secret that stays on this computer, so it identifies nothing else.
diagnostic.never: The file name or folder, your user or computer name, dates, any text from the file (references, net names, part numbers, values, titles, comments), coordinates or dimensions, raw bytes, keys, or anything you type.
diagnostic.level2Hint: More detail for the developers. It also reveals a little more about the file. Off by default.
diagnostic.dedupeHint: Helps the developers notice the same file sent twice. Off by default.
diagnostic.risk: Remaining risk: counts rounded to two digits, the size range and the file variant can still hint at which board family a file belongs to. Level 2 adds more of this. Read the report below before you share it.
diagnostic.reportTitle: The report, exactly as it will be saved
diagnostic.saved: Saved. Attach the file to your format request on GitHub or paste its text into the form. Nothing was sent anywhere.
diagnostic.saveFailed: The report could not be saved.
diagnostic.outcomeFailed: TRACE recognised this file but could not open it.
diagnostic.outcomeUnrecognized: TRACE did not recognise this file.
diagnostic.bugDescriptionHint: Briefly describe what you expected and what happened. Do not include passwords, customer details or file paths.
diagnostic.bugSendOnlyHint: Sent privately to TRACE support through Cloudflare only when you select Send. No files are attached.
diagnostic.bugMinimalData: Technical details contain only a small set of coarse app and import facts. Your description is the only free text sent.
diagnostic.bugProviderMetadata: Cloudflare receives connection metadata. A short-lived hashed IP bucket is used for abuse control and deleted within 48 hours.
diagnostic.bugRetention: Reports are kept for up to 30 days. Cloudflare D1 recovery history may retain deleted content for up to 7 more days.
diagnostic.bugDraftLocalInfo: Optional drafts and retry records stay on this device only and expire after 7 days.
diagnostic.bugDraftExpired: This draft or retry record has expired and was removed.
diagnostic.bugStorageUnavailable: Local storage is unavailable. Nothing was sent; copy your text or try again later.
diagnostic.bugUnconfirmed: Delivery could not be confirmed. It may already have been received. Retry checks the same report safely.
diagnostic.bugRetryAfter: You can try again in {seconds} seconds.
diagnostic.bugEditedAfterAttempt: After a send attempt, editing creates a new report. Review it again before sending.
diagnostic.bugReviewReplacement: Review the proposed replacements before sending. Detection may miss private details.
diagnostic.bugWebUnavailable: Report sending is unavailable in the web version. Your text stays here.
diagnostic.bugBridgeUnavailable: Report sending is unavailable in this app session. Your text stays here.
diagnostic.bugErrorOffline: No internet connection. Your report is still here; try again when you are online.
diagnostic.bugErrorTimeout: The request timed out. Delivery could not be confirmed.
diagnostic.bugErrorCancelled: Sending was cancelled. The report may already have been received.
diagnostic.bugErrorInvalid: The report could not be validated. Review it and try again.
diagnostic.bugErrorTooLarge: The report is too large to send.
diagnostic.bugErrorRateLimited: Too many reports were sent recently. Try again later.
diagnostic.bugErrorUnavailable: The report service is unavailable. Your report is still here; try again later.
diagnostic.bugErrorStorage: The report could not be saved on this device, so it was not sent.
diagnostic.bugErrorConflict: This report conflicts with an earlier send attempt. Review it before trying again.
diagnostic.bugErrorUnknown: The report could not be sent. Your text is still here; try again later.
diagnostic.bugErrorBusy: A report is already being sent. Wait for it to finish.
diagnostic.bugErrorStalePreview: The report changed. Review the latest version before sending.
diagnostic.bugCleanupTiming: These limits assume normal scheduled cleanup; hosting outages may delay deletion.
